body.title: Hypothermia
body.html:
Hypothermia is defined as a body core temperature below 35.0 °C (95.0 °F) in humans. Symptoms depend on the temperature.

Signs and symptoms

In mild hypothermia, there is shivering and mental confusion. In moderate hypothermia, shivering stops and confusion increases.

Management

Treatment of mild hypothermia involves warm drinks, warm clothing, and voluntary physical activity. In those with moderate hypothermia, heating blankets and warmed intravenous fluids are recommended. Rescuers should handle the person gently, since rough movement can trigger a dangerous heart rhythm.

body.title: Frostbite
body.html: Frostbite is a skin injury that occurs when exposed to extreme low temperatures, most commonly in the fingers, toes, nose and ears. Rewarming should not be done by rubbing the skin.

body.title: Space blanket
body.html: A space blanket is an especially low-weight, low-bulk blanket made of heat-reflective thin plastic sheeting, used to reduce heat loss from a person's body.

message.content:
Warm the person **gradually** and handle them gently [1].

1. **Get out of the cold.** Move them somewhere sheltered and give them warm clothing [1].
2. **Insulate.** A space blanket is a light, heat-reflective sheet that reduces heat loss [3].
3. **Warm drinks** if they are alert and can swallow [1].
4. **Don't rub the skin.** Rough movement can trigger a dangerous heart rhythm, and frostbitten skin shouldn't be rubbed [1][2].

If shivering stops and confusion increases, that is **moderate hypothermia**: heating blankets and warmed intravenous fluids are recommended, so get help as fast as you can [1].
